x: Rashmi College of Physiotherapy (RCP) is a health-science college on Sandur Road, Kudligi, in the Vijayanagara district of Karnataka. We offer the Bachelor of Physiotherapy (BPT) , affiliated to Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences (RGUHS), Bengaluru , with an annual intake of 40 students. RGUHS Affiliated university · College code PT113 BPT Bachelor of Physiotherapy · 4 years + 1-year internship 40 seats Annual intake (RGUHS, 2025–26 onwards) NCAHP Competency-Based Curriculum for Physiotherapy (2025) Who we are Physiotherapy is an autonomous, first-contact, science-based healthcare profession. Physiotherapists assess, diagnose and treat problems of movement and function caused by injury, disease, ageing or disability, and they promote health and fitness across the lifespan, from newborns to older adults. RCP was set up to bring quality physiotherapy education to North Karnataka. India is seeing more chronic disease, an ageing population and more lifestyle-related illness, and the national curriculum notes that demand for rehabilitation is growing in rural and urban areas alike. Our graduates are trained to meet that need in hospitals and clinics, and also in primary health centres, schools, workplaces and homes. The college is run by Sri Siddalingeshwara Education Trust , the same management as our sister institution, the Rashmi Institute of Ayurveda Medical Sciences & Research Center (RIA) , Kudligi. Two health-science institutions under one management give our students a wider academic community and a shared commitment to the health of the region. Hands-on assessment and treatment skills are at the heart of the BPT programme. What we teach, and how Our BPT programme follows the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions (NCAHP) Competency-Based Curriculum for Physiotherapy (2025) , issued under the NCAHP Act, 2021 by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, within the regulations of RGUHS. The curriculum moves beyond what a student knows to what a graduate can do . Integrated learning Basic sciences are linked to clinical practice from the first year, and subjects are taught around shared, clinically relevant themes. Early clinical exposure Clinic orientation in Year 1, then clinical observation, clinical education and clinical rotation, before a 12-month internship. Skills labs & simulation Students practise on peers, mannequins and simulators before they treat patients, under the Demonstrate–Observe–Assist–Perform model. Competency-based assessment OSCE, OSPE, DOPS, case presentations and continuous internal assessment measure real clinical ability. Our approach Patient first. Respect for each patient's autonomy, privacy and dignity, and fair access to care for all. Evidence-based. Research methodology, biostatistics and evidence-based practice are part of the core course, with a supervised project during internship. Community-minded. Field visits to rural and urban PHCs, health camps, disability screening and a two-month rural posting during internship. Team players. Students learn to work with doctors, nurses, occupational therapists, speech therapists and other allied health professionals. Lifelong learners. Self-directed learning and reflective practice prepare graduates for further study (MPT, PhD) and continuing education. x: The Bachelor of Physiotherapy (BPT) at Rashmi College of Physiotherapy is a 5-year programme : four academic years on an annual pattern, followed by a one-year compulsory rotatory internship. It is affiliated to RGUHS, Bengaluru and follows the NCAHP Competency-Based Curriculum for Physiotherapy (2025) . Where RGUHS or State regulations differ from the national curriculum, the University and State regulations prevail. 5 years 4 academic years + 1-year rotatory internship 40 seats Annual intake 36 courses Across four academic years 334 credits National Credit Framework 6,240 hours Of teaching across four years (1,560 a year) 2,016+ hours Minimum internship hours in the fifth year Curriculum background Quality treatment is central to physiotherapy. It depends on a sound knowledge of the basic sciences and of how physiotherapy techniques and procedures interact. As technology and techniques grow more complex, the physiotherapist's role and responsibility keep growing. The BPT gives students the scientific and theoretical foundation of the profession and trains them to synthesise, evaluate and apply that knowledge in clinical settings. The curriculum aims to produce physiotherapists who are: Technically and clinically competent to make independent decisions Competent to assess a patient Aware of patient conditions and treatment, and of the importance of quality assurance Grounded in the theory behind evidence-based practice Effective members of the multidisciplinary team Prepared to take part in, or start, research into practice The curriculum was built by looking at every area of physiotherapy and at the roles expected of physiotherapists at different levels of experience, with the aim of connecting education with employment practice. A Foundation Course brings all students to the same understanding of basic healthcare norms before they begin. Clinical practice starts in the second year and continues as a rotation between theory and practice throughout the programme. Programme outcomes As an independent practitioner, an entry-level physiotherapy graduate will be able to: Provide quality care to individuals and populations to optimise their movement, function and quality of life. Examine, assess, evaluate, treat and prescribe physiotherapeutic management for diseases, disorders and trauma conditions. Promote health and use strategies based on the best available research evidence to prevent and minimise impairments, activity limitations and participation restrictions. Provide ethical care through high standards of professional practice. Communicate effectively to strengthen therapeutic and professional relationships. Prescribe and understand diagnostic imaging, electrophysiological, haematological and biochemistry investigations for diagnosis, treatment or referral to other healthcare professionals. Integrate the best available research evidence into clinical decision-making and practice. Show commitment to continuous learning and scholarly activity. Work effectively with the healthcare team to provide patient-centred care. Manage self, time, resources and priorities to deliver safe, effective and sustainable services. Demonstrate competence in quality assurance relevant to physiotherapy practice. Learning objectives By the end of the course, the student should be able to: Acquire the cognitive, affective and psychomotor skills needed to examine, evaluate, diagnose, plan, carry out and document physiotherapy treatment, independently or with the multidisciplinary team. Evaluate patients for impairments and functional limitations, and carry out all routine physiotherapeutic procedures based on that evaluation. Operate and maintain physiotherapy equipment, and plan and deliver treatment (both electrotherapy and exercise therapy) independently. Educate patients and caregivers about health promotion, disease and disorder prevention, and physiotherapeutic interventions. Demonstrate all the competencies needed to achieve the programme out

x: Physiotherapy students learn their most important lessons with patients. Year 1 · Clinic Orientation & Visit (BPT-110) · 150 hours Part of the foundation course. Students visit the whole chain of healthcare delivery: sub-centre, PHC, CHC, sub-district and district hospitals, a medical college, and private hospitals and clinics. They also meet the village panchayat and front-line health workers. Year 2 · Clinical Observation (BPT-209) · 210 hours Rotating postings in physiotherapy OPDs and hospital wards, where students observe patient care and keep a case portfolio or diary. Year 3 · Clinical Education (BPT-308) · 300 hours Supervised training in wards and OPDs: bedside approach, assessment, special tests, indications and contraindications, treatment dosage and outcome measures. Case presentations, case discussions and critique enquiry become a regular part of learning. Year 4 · Clinical Rotation (BPT-409) · 390 hours A supervised rotation through ten clinical areas. Students decide treatment parameters and dosage, use outcome measures and apply evidence-based practice for real patients. Year 5 · Rotatory Clinical Internship · 12 months Full-time postings averaging 7 hours a day, 6 days a week, for a minimum of 2,016 hours, including a 2-month rural posting. Interns keep a log book, present at least twelve cases and complete a supervised project. About the internship . Skills before patients. Every practical skill is first taught in the laboratories with the DOAP model (Demonstrate, Observe, Assist, Perform), and special tests are practised on a healthy model before they are used on patients. Competence is assessed at rising levels, from knows and knows how to shows how and finally performs independently . This page describes the BPT and the further study and career routes open to BPT graduates under the national curriculum. Programme offered Undergraduate · Admissions 2026–27 Bachelor of Physiotherapy (BPT) A five-year professional degree affiliated to RGUHS, Bengaluru, and taught to the NCAHP Competency-Based Curriculum for Physiotherapy (2025). Students build a strong scientific base in the early years, move steadily into supervised clinical work and finish with a year-long rotatory internship. The MPT, PhD and clinical fellowships described below are not offered at RCP. They are shown here as the career pathway after BPT, as set out in the NCAHP Curriculum Handbook of Physiotherapy (2025). Career pathway after BPT There is one entry pathway into the profession, the bachelor's degree. From there, the national curriculum sets out a ladder of further qualifications. BPT: Bachelor of Physiotherapy Offered at RCP Eligibility: 10+2 (or equivalent) with Physics, Chemistry and Biology, minimum 50% aggregate in PCB; must have appeared in NEET; minimum age 17 years. Duration: 5 years, including a 1-year full-time rotatory internship. Prepares an independent healthcare practitioner who can diagnose, plan, deliver and quality-assure physiotherapy care. MPT: Master of Physiotherapy Eligibility: BPT from a recognised university with pass marks (50%); entrance test and interview. Duration: 2 years (at least 3,240 hours). Specialised postgraduate study; postgraduates are expected to contribute significantly to research and academics. PhD in Physiotherapy Eligibility: full-time postgraduate degree in physiotherapy, minimum 55%; selection on merit in a university entrance exam. Duration: full-time 3 years (maximum 5); part-time 4 years (maximum 6). Original research in an elective field; not available by distance or online mode. Clinical Fellowship Eligibility: registered with NCAHP, at least 1 year of experience in a related subject, and a written and/or oral entrance exam. Duration: at least 12 months. Structured training in a sub-specialty at an academic institute or hospital, with a logbook and project. It does not lead to a postgraduate degree. The emphasis moves from science to specialty as the course progresses. Year 1: Foundations Anatomy, physiology and biochemistry, the fundamentals of exercise and electro-physical agents, foundation subjects such as communication and the healthcare system, and clinic orientation visits. Year 4: Specialties Neurology, cardiothoracic care, sports physiotherapy, community rehabilitation, ethics and management, project work orientation, and a clinical rotation through every specialty. Year 5: Rotatory internship Twelve months of supervised postings across musculoskeletal, neurological, cardiopulmonary, community, sports, paediatric and women's health physiotherapy. d: What physiotherapists do, where they work and why India needs them: scope of practice, the 'Dr … PT' title, ISCO 2264, job roles and career areas.
x: Physiotherapy covers the whole range of care, from health promotion and prevention through to rehabilitation, for individuals and for whole populations at every stage of life. This page explains the role of the physiotherapist as described in the NCAHP Curriculum Handbook of Physiotherapy (2025), the national curriculum that RCP follows. About physiotherapy Physiotherapists diagnose movement dysfunction through careful examination and evaluation, whatever its cause. They then give skilled therapeutic treatment to improve physical function and help each person reach the best possible quality of life. They combine detailed knowledge of the human body and how it works with specialised hands-on clinical skills. They use these to assess, diagnose and treat physical problems caused by disorders, illness, injury, trauma or disability. Physiotherapists work independently and as members of the multidisciplinary rehabilitation and habilitation team. After the necessary assessment, evaluation and investigations, they prescribe and carry out treatment programmes that help people gain, keep or regain the best possible function. A first point of contact. Physiotherapists are an essential part of primary care: people with impairments or functional limitations can come to a physiotherapist directly as their way into the healthcare system. Physiotherapists also refer patients to other professionals and receive referrals from them, and work as case managers, teachers, researchers and consultants. What physiotherapists do Physiotherapists follow their own code of ethical principles. Their work may include any of the following: Promote health Promoting the health and well-being of individuals and the public, with emphasis on physical activity and exercise. Prevent Preventing impairments, activity limitations, participation restrictions and disabilities in people whose movement is at risk from health, socio-economic, environmental or lifestyle factors. Assess and diagnose Evaluating the person, prescribing the investigations needed to diagnose physical dysfunction, and prescribing physiotherapy treatment plans. Treat Restoring the body systems essential to movement, maximising function and recovery, minimising incapacity, and improving quality of life, independent living and the ability to work. Remove barriers Adapting environmental, home and workplace access so that people can take full part in their normal roles in society. Shape policy Contributing to local, national and international health policies and public health strategies. Scope and need for physiotherapists in India Healthcare is moving quickly towards a patient-centred model delivered by multidisciplinary teams. India faces more chronic disease, an ageing population and more lifestyle-related illness, so demand for rehabilitative and therapeutic services is growing fast. Physiotherapists improve patients' quality of life by promoting mobility, managing pain and building functional independence, which also reduces the load on medical and surgical treatment. As the Government of India works towards Universal Health Coverage and expands hospitals, clinics, wellness centres and academic institutions, physiotherapists are essential members of multidisciplinary teams at every level of healthcare delivery. Growing awareness of preventive healthcare is increasing demand in both rural and urban areas. For example, the National guidelines for prevention and management of stroke note that physiotherapists greatly improve the management of stroke survivors and help them return to normal life sooner. d: Vision, mission, core values and commitment to excellence of Rashmi College of Physiotherapy, Kudligi.
x: Our vision and mission flow from the purpose of physiotherapy itself: to help every person achieve the best possible movement, function and quality of life. Vision To be a centre of excellence in physiotherapy education in North Karnataka, producing competent, compassionate and evidence-based physiotherapists who carry rehabilitation from the hospital to every home and village. Mission Deliver the BPT through competency-based, student-centred teaching with early and continuous clinical exposure. Develop the knowledge, skills and attitudes for independent, ethical practice as first-contact practitioners. Serve rural and under-served communities through outreach, screening and community-based rehabilitation. Build a culture of enquiry, research and lifelong learning among students and faculty. Core values Compassion We see the person behind every patient and treat everyone with empathy and respect. Integrity Honesty, accountability and confidentiality in the classroom, the clinic and the community. Evidence Clinical decisions grounded in the best available research and careful assessment. Teamwork Shared goals with patients, families and the multidisciplinary health team. Equity Fair, unbiased access to care, and inclusion of persons with disabilities. Excellence High standards of professional practice and a commitment to keep improving. Graduate attributes The NCAHP curriculum organises learning goals into key areas. Every RCP graduate should be able to demonstrate: Independent clinical practice A patient- and family-centred approach, using the best available evidence to plan preventive, investigative and management plans, prescribe investigations, interventions and assistive devices, and recognise when to refer. Communication Clear, empathetic communication with patients, caregivers, colleagues and the community, including accurate, timely records and counselling on lifestyle change. Membership of a multidisciplinary team Shared goals, clear roles, mutual trust and the use of measurable outcomes and feedback to improve team performance. Ethics and accountability Applying clinical ethics and legal concepts to practice; respecting autonomy, privacy and confidentiality; fair and unbiased access to care. Commitment to professional excellence Competence, empathy, integrity and a non-judgemental attitude, with accountability to patients, peers, employers and regulators. Leadership and mentorship Acting as an agent of change in quality improvement, managing time and resources, and coordinating, delegating and supervising care safely. Social accountability Understanding the determinants of health, responding to population health needs and advocating for the services patients need. Lifelong learning Objective self-assessment, continual skill improvement, critical evaluation of the literature and a rewarding career pathway.
